title: Nathan Cleary headlines Aussie stars at UFC 312 - as the Panthers halfback reveals why he thinks MMA 'is nothing like any other sport'
text:
The NRL star, Nathan Cleary, was one of the multiple Australian sports stars seen in the Qudos Bank event for the UFC 312 event on Sunday.
The controversial American star, who had previously attacked against Australia calling the “communist” government, was defeated in a brutal and bloody fighter by the South African fighter Dricus du Plessis in the main event.
Du Plessis broke his opponent’s nose while he won a unanimous decision victory against Strickland in his revenge, to retain his medium weight title.
Faced with record assistance in an inner Australian sand, Zhang Weili defended Tatian ANSHUL JUJI.
He produced a prolific knockout in his debut fight with a large right above the right, sending his opponent to the canvas with the referee who finished the contest.
Cleary was one of several high profile names within the Qudos Bank Arena and met with the president of UFC, Dana White, during the night and sat next to his fellow NRL stars of NRL Hudson Young and Scott Sorensen.

“Yes, pumped, I came the last time I was also in Sydney, so I’m happy to be here again and enjoy it,” said Footy star to the outlet when he arrived at the place.

‘Quite regularly. I have been in that for a while and I love elite sport and see them do their own and when they enter that octagon, it’s nothing about another sport.
